correctness.rationale: For r>=max arm length, deleting the hub leaves a simplex. The link is exactly the prefix-length inequality Σq_i≤r−1. For faces lacking an internal arm vertex, toggling a terminal leaf beyond the first deficiency preserves all constraints and gives an acyclic fiberwise matching, contracting A. Remaining relative faces U∪J form a truncated augmented exterior simplex chain complex; ∂=contraction by the sum functional, so top homology is det(Z[U])⊗Λ^t ker(sum:Z^k→Z), t=r−B−1. With B≥k≥3 the quotient K/A is simply connected with free homology in a single degree; Hurewicz and Whitehead give the wedge type and hub suspension shifts it to S^{r−1}. At t<0 the link contracts; at r≥|V| it is the full simplex. Signs under equal-length arm permutations follow the oriented relative complex. The finite 59-case checker corroborates only, not proving the all-parameter statement.
residual_risks: The ordinary wedge equivalence is not an equivariant splitting; there is no claim for r<max arm length.
